text:
Priya K: FYI — sales just forwarded a big ask from HorizonHealth. They want a committed reserved capacity + deep per-token discount for embeddings and generation, plus a defined overage credit system. Sales is asking for guidance on packaging and whether this should go to backlog or be handled as a bespoke deal.
Samir: copy. do we have margins for that kind of discount? also what counts as 'embeddings' vs 'generation' in their usage pattern?
Eli: they mentioned heavy embedding usage for similarity search (>70% of tokens). generation is occasional. if embeddings are the main driver, we could propose a blended embedding unit rate separate from text gen.
Marcos: timeline question — Sales wants pricing and a proposal by EOD Friday. that's tight. We should be realistic about what product can commit to.
Billing Bot: New ticket created: #HH-4521 — "HorizonHealth committed capacity & discount ask". Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/HH-4521
Rashida: from finops POV, we need a lower bound on per-unit price that keeps gross margin >= 35% after reserved infra costs + burst cushion. Can product give an estimate of cost per 1M embedding units on Dedicated?
Priya K: Good question. Engineering — can you ballpark infra cost for 1M embedding units (quantized model on A100-level or ampere equivalent) vs 1M text gen tokens? rough numbers ok.
Eli: rough calc: optimized quantized embed model on A10x or similar: ~ $18 / 1M embeddings at current reserved amortized rates. Text gen (small-medium sequences) ~ $25 - $40 / 1M tokens depending on context length and KV cache hit. these are very workload-sensitive.
Samir: ok thanks. So if finance wants 35% margin, list price must be >= $27 for embeddings to be safe. that's high vs market for embeddings.
Marcos: competitive note — some vendors offer sub-$10 equivalent embedding pricing but without reserved capacity SLAs. HorizonHealth is specifically asking for SLA + private VPC. That's where value could justify premium.
Priya K: Thinking in product terms: options include (A) bespoke enterprise quote (sales-handled; not in public packaging), (B) create a formal "Reserved Embedding Pack" product (docs, SKU, rollout) or (C) a hybrid — short pilot reserved commit + trial discounted credits for overage. Which should we prioritize?
Rashida: (A) fastest to close but operational overhead long-term. (B) requires roadmap work: SKU, billing flows, Console UI, RBAC for reserved. (C) could be quick if we limit to 3 months pilot with automated rollback.
Eli: engineering effort estimates: (A) low dev: just manual metering + invoice credit. (B) medium-high: billing automation, new routing policy for reserved pools, console pages. (C) medium: pilot automation + temporary flags.
Samir: Sales says HorizonHealth wants an annual commit but willing to start pilot. I'd argue (C) gets the deal and buys time for product to build (B).
Priya K: Agree. For product backlog, my recommendation: create an RFC for "Reserved Embedding Pack" (epic) with two-phase delivery: pilot (3mo) -> GA. Pilot scope: custom pricing, manual contract + automated crediting; no immediate console support. GA scope: SKU + console + SLA metadata + billing flow.
Marcos: Launch criteria for pilot? I'd add: 1) handshake with sales + signed pilot contract; 2) infra runbook for reserved pool provisioning; 3) billing credit automation in staging; 4) monitoring dashboard for token usage and cost.
Priya K: I'll file the RFC and tag it P1 for Q2 planning, but estimate P2 for overall roadmap because full productization is Q3 work. Action items: Rashida to provide margin floor numbers, Eli to sketch infra runbook and provisioning time, Samir to secure signed pilot contract draft, Marcos to outline monitoring metrics.
Rashida: will send margin floor and a simple excel modeling LOE by EOD tomorrow.
Eli: I'll put a short infra note in the RFC with provisioning SLA options: 24h warm start vs 72h cold start and cost delta.
Samir: I'll coordinate with legal for pilot T&Cs and ping SalesOps.
Priya K: Perfect. For backlog triage: creating HH-4521 as an umbrella with subtask RFC-1719 (Reserved Embedding Pack RFC). I'll mark the initial pilot work as backlog P1 but not schedule until contract signed.
Marcos: optional product tweak: offer a small buffer of preloaded "burst credits" that can be used while reserved pool boots to avoid immediate overage spikes. low dev, high perceived value.
Priya K: love that. include as pilot experiment.
Samir: one more ask from sales — customer also asked whether overage credits can be auto-applied vs manual invoice. can we commit pilot to automated crediting?
Eli: we can auto-apply credits for pilot using a simple multiplier rule in billing pipeline; low complexity.
Priya K: Ok. Final call: proceed with pilot (C) as recommended. Product will own RFC + acceptance criteria. Sales can offer bespoke price for pilot once Rashida confirms margin floor.
Marcos: noted. I'll add monitoring acceptance tests to RFC.
Billing Bot: Ticket HH-4521 updated: RFC-1719 linked.
Priya K: Thanks everyone. I'll drop a short summary to sales and cc Legal/Finance.
